# RETRO: t4 PR #12164

## What worked
- Downloading Arch's exact binary package (Opus) and static analysis of the packaged sudoers.so (Sol) settled the mail_badpass dispute without real sudo.
- A neutral cross-examination follow-up turned Sol's unexamined "mail_badpass changes behavior" claim into an independently verified no-op, and gave independent confirmation of the override behavior and branch context.

## Process deviations (recorded, not blocking)
- Opus reviewer: two parallel WORKFLOW.md reads exceeded the 60-line aggregate bound (complete, not truncated); one host-side `python3 -c` JSON parse and one `file -b` on downloaded data outside review.py; review.py git preflight run against shared pinned worktree with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1 (HEAD/clean re-checked); a 404 Debian fetch kept and unused.
- Sol reviewer: first review.py init lacked --fixture (usage error only); one read of 55 lines instead of 50; early read-only binary probes did not set and read back core limit; one mistyped plan path failed before launch.
- Coordinator: used `cut -c1-400` once to display `subagents` JSON output (metadata, not policy/source; no content truncated since lines were short). Read one sibling team's brief (t2-12167) for format only; briefs are neutral by rule and contained no PR conclusions.

## Friction / tool ideas
- review.py lacks a synthetic passwd option, which blocks safe `visudo -c` experiments (feature request).
- Sol's runtime has no network, so upstream source and PKGBUILD could not be fetched; Opus had network fetch. Asymmetric source access between reviewers (feature request: approved read-only fetch for Sol).
- Bash redirections in PR tests cannot be wrapper-guarded; inventory and retention were used instead.

## Carry forward
- For "hardening" PRs, check the shipped package's compiled defaults first; many flags are already default.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

On the sudo that Arch currently ships (1.9.17p2), all three `Defaults` lines in the new drop-in are either already in effect or have no effect, so the file does not change sudo behavior on a stock Omarchy system. Its one observable effect is that it overrides opt-outs a user places in `/etc/sudoers`. **Verified:** the PR's claim that existing timeout and retry policies are preserved holds (`passwd_tries=10` and the faillock settings are untouched), and `test/sudo-hardening-test.sh` passes at the PR head.

### The drop-in restates existing sudo defaults

| Line added | Arch sudo 1.9.17p2 without the drop-in | With the drop-in |
|---|---|---|
| `Defaults env_reset` | already on (compile-time default; the packaged `sudoers(5)` says "on by default") | on, no change |
| `Defaults use_pty` | already on (default since sudo 1.9.14) | on, no change |
| `Defaults mail_badpass` | off | flag on, but no mail is sent: the packaged `sudoers.so` has no mailer path compiled in, so the mail routine returns early, and Omarchy's package list installs no MTA |

**Impact:** the description ("enforcing environment resetting, pty allocation for command isolation") suggests protection that stock systems already have. `mail_badpass` stays inert unless an administrator also sets `mailerpath` and installs a mail transport.

**Suggested change:** if the intent is to pin current defaults explicitly, say so in the description and consider leaving out `mail_badpass` (or pair it with a `mailerpath`). Otherwise the drop-in may not be needed.

### The drop-in overrides opt-outs made in `/etc/sudoers`

Arch's packaged `/etc/sudoers` ends with `@includedir /etc/sudoers.d`, and sudo applies generic, user and runas `Defaults` entries in file order, with later entries overriding earlier ones (`sudoers(5)`: "later entries will override earlier ones").

```text
/etc/sudoers
  line 80   # Defaults>root !use_pty      <- shipped commented; an admin uncomments it
  ...
  line 139  @includedir /etc/sudoers.d
              99-omarchy-hardening:  Defaults use_pty   <- parsed later, wins
Result: use_pty stays on for root; the documented opt-out no longer works
```

The same applies to `Defaults:user !use_pty` or `Defaults !env_reset` in the main file. Only entries placed after the `@includedir` line, command-specific `Defaults!cmd` entries, or drop-ins that sort after `99-omarchy-hardening` could still opt out. Note that `99-` does not mean "last": sudo sorts `sudoers.d` names bytewise, so this file loads before Omarchy's letter-named drop-ins such as `passwd-tries`.

**Impact:** a user who follows the Arch template to disable `use_pty` for root sees no effect, with no obvious reason. This is established from sudo's source, documentation and the packaged plugin, not from a live sudo run.

**Suggested change:** if explicit pins are kept, document that local overrides need a later-sorting drop-in or a command-specific `Defaults` entry.

### Existing installs do not receive the file

The script is only called from `install/config/all.sh`, which runs on fresh installs. Updates run `migrations/*.sh`, and this PR adds no migration, so upgraded systems never get `/etc/sudoers.d/99-omarchy-hardening`. Fresh installs also take `master` by default (`boot.sh` checks out `dev` only with `OMARCHY_REF=dev`), and the package-based Quattro upgrade installs its own `omarchy-*` sudoers files and does not call this script.

**Impact:** fresh and upgraded v3 systems would differ, and Quattro systems are not reached.

**Suggested change:** if the change is kept, add a migration per the repository's install/migration convention, and carry the setting into the Quattro settings package if it is wanted there.

**Optional:** the script installs the file first and validates afterwards, and `visudo -cf ... || sudo rm -f ...` exits 0 either way, so a rollback is logged as a completed step with no reason. With this fixed content the rollback cannot trigger, but validating a temporary file and then installing it with `install -m 0440`, or logging the rollback, would make failures visible.

**Optional test improvement:** in an isolated run, four changes to the script still pass the test: commenting out `Defaults use_pty`, adding an invalid option, changing the mode to `666`, and deleting the validation line. The stub `sudo` also forwards unrecognized commands to the host, so a failing `visudo` stub turns the rollback into `rm -f` on the real `/etc/sudoers.d/99-omarchy-hardening` path. Whole-line matches (`grep -Fxq`), a `chmod` stub that records and asserts `440`, and a stub `else` branch that fails instead of running `"$@"` would close these gaps.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of the PR head (`9eeed287`) and the Omarchy install, update and migration code it touches; sudo 1.9.17p2 source and documentation; and Arch's packaged `sudo 1.9.17.p2-6` (default `/etc/sudoers`, man page and static analysis of `sudoers.so`). The PR's test and mutated copies of the script ran in an isolated sandbox. Real `sudo` and `visudo` were not run, so the override behavior and the missing mailer path are established from source, documentation and the packaged binary, not from live `sudo -V` output. The Omarchy ISO's own sudoers edits and the Quattro settings package source were not inspected.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up on disputed points, and an Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
